description: Creates a GDScript file, or adds functions, variables and signals to one. Every declaration written carries a type. Both load what they wrote under the project's own warning settings and answer with parses; the engine's reasons for a refusal come back under engine_messages. create answers with the extends and class_name the engine read, and a script declaring a class_name is put in the project's class list, with registered saying whether it is there. modify makes every addition or none, and answers with the line each one is on in the file written. rename renames a class or a member wherever the engine uses it and writes every file or none. A new name already taken is refused with nothing written, a member's included when a class inheriting it already uses the name in code, as a local or a parameter. changed lists each file with its changed lines as they now read, and leftAlone lists every other whole-word occurrence of the old name with what the tokenizer makes of it (code, string, comment, doc, nodePath, scene, text, or ignored for a file under a .gdignore directory, which is never changed) and, where it is not plain, why: a string that is the old name whole, such as find_children's type or a call's method name, which nothing renames or compiles and which is listed first; a node named like the class; a call on a value whose type the analyser could not tell. A member rename answers under languageServer how many requests it made and how long they took. A comment, documentation line, string or text file line with nothing more to say is given under leftAloneInProse by file, kind and line instead, and code that is certainly another symbol of the same name, a bare name in a file where nothing inherits the member or one the language server resolved to another declaration, under leftAloneOtherSymbols as each why with the files and lines it covers. summary.leftAlone counts each of the three lists beside the total. Read both before calling the rename done; nothing in them was changed. Afterwards an open editor scans the changed files and reloads every changed script, which is also the compile check, and its answer comes back under editor; with no editor the class cache is rebuilt and the changed scripts are compiled in a fresh engine, under classCache and compiled. written is true once the files are written, and ok is false when what came after the write failed: the files are left changed, and note says so. Operations: create: a new script file; modify (needs modifications): add to an existing script; rename (needs symbol, newName): rename a class or a member wherever the engine uses it, across the project.

className.description: create: a class_name for the script. Not with content.

content.description: create: the whole file, written as given, instead of a template, className and extends.

extends.description: create: the base class. Default Node. Not with content.

defaultValue.description: Variables: the initial value, as written in GDScript.

exportHint.description: Variables: the export hint, such as "range(0, 100)".

params.description: Functions and signals: the parameter list, "delta: float".

newScriptPath.description: rename: also move the declaring script here, with its .uid beside it, rewriting every string that names it by path in the same style it was written (res:// or relative), and the relative paths in the moved script itself.

preview.description: rename: answer with what would change and what would be left alone, and write nothing. Default false.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

scriptPath.description: Script file inside the project, such as "scripts/player.gd".

symbol.description: rename: what to rename, declared by the script at scriptPath: its class_name, or a method, variable, constant, signal, enum, enum value or inner class at its top level. A class is renamed from the files and needs no editor: every bare use in code, the declaration, doc links such as [Told] and [method Told.say], and the script_class a .tres records. A script that declares something of its own by the old name, and a use after a dot, are left alone, since which of those mean the class cannot be told from the text. A member is renamed from what the editor's language server resolves to it, so it needs the editor open on this project; a method is renamed together with every override of it in the classes inheriting it, and from the topmost class declaring it when scriptPath's is itself an override. Doc links naming the member through any class inheriting it are renamed too, and so are a scene's or resource's saved value of a variable on a node or resource whose script inherits it, and a connection naming the signal on its emitter or the method on its receiver. A name the engine itself declares on the native base, such as _ready, is refused, as is a new name already taken: by a class, an autoload, an identifier in code, a native class or built-in type, or a member anywhere in the class's chain.

name: script_edit
